result.summary: This is a narrow residential street with a sidewalk present only on one side of the roadway. The environment is characterized by high levels of on-street parking and a lack of formal pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: There is no sidewalk on the right side of the street, forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the white wall

hazards.name: Narrow Walkway
hazards.description: The existing sidewalk on the left is very narrow and bordered by dense vegetation, making it difficult for pedestrians to pass one another.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars on both sides of the narrow street limit sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: New Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install a continuous paved sidewalk on the right side of the street to provide a dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or speed cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low on this narrow residential block.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near the end of the block to improve visibility for pedestrians entering the roadway.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a continuous concrete sidewalk separated from the roadway by a narrow grass buffer. A long blank wall on one side and an open field on the other create a somewhat isolated environment with limited natural surveillance.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: A long, high wall creates a lack of 'eyes on the street' and can make pedestrians feel isolated or trapped.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, bordering the sidewalk

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: The parked car obscures the sightline between a pedestrian stepping off the curb and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, blue car parked at the curb

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and perceived safety at night.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Plant street trees in the grass buffer to provide shade, improve aesthetics, and provide a physical sense of protection from traffic.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: If there is significant pedestrian demand for the open field, a marked mid-block crossing with signage should be considered.

result.summary: A residential street featuring sidewalks on both sides, with a park on the left and row houses on the right. While the environment is low-speed, the high density of parked cars creates significant visual obstructions for pedestrians crossing mid-block.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street limits sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway throughout the visible block.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to increase pedestrian visibility and reduce the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked mid-block crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a designated crossing point between the residential area and the park.

result.summary: This is a narrow residential street with a continuous paved sidewalk and mature vegetation. While the low-speed environment is generally safe, the lack of a buffer between the walkway and parked vehicles creates potential visibility issues for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked car and covered motorcycles block sightlines between the sidewalk and the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and midground along the curb

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The narrow sidewalk is directly adjacent to the curb with no physical separation from the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the property line

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near potential crossing points to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer
interventions.description: Incorporate a planting strip or street furniture to provide a physical and psychological barrier between the walkway and the street.
